themes.persistence: localStorage 'theme', applied by a beforeInteractive script in layout.tsx before first paint
themes.mechanism: globals.css rebinds Tailwind slate-50..900, white, red, green, amber and blue-700 to --c-* variables in @theme inline; each --c-* is defined once per theme. In dark, slate is inverted (slate-50 = ground, slate-800 = porcelain ink, white = raised enamel).

display.purpose: Course name as a line sign in a 2px porcelain frame.

figure-hero.purpose: The 'ต้องได้อีก' points-needed readout; the largest number on the page.

figure-board.purpose: Points earned on the departure board; secondary board figures at 1.5rem.

figure-station.purpose: Per-station score, right-aligned, with muted '/ max'.

body.purpose: Station names, forecast headlines, terminus captions (Thai).

body-sm.purpose: Tabs, hints, row labels, forecast detail.

label-code.purpose: K / P / A category code before the Thai category name.

wordmark.purpose: Uppercase 'KruKhayan Physics' in the header only.

shadows.name: route-glow
shadows.value: drop-shadow(0 0 6px color-mix(in oklch, currentColor calc(var(--glow-strength) * 100%), transparent))
shadows.purpose: Neon bleed on graded rail segments and filled station discs only; --glow-strength 0.55 dark, 0 light. Applied as filter, not box-shadow.

focus.name: focus-ring
focus.purpose: Global :focus-visible; light theme swaps outline-color to var(--line-cobalt).

focus.name: selection
focus.value: background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--line-cobalt) 45%, transparent); color: var(--c-slate-900)

motion.name: rail-reveal
motion.purpose: Enamel cover over the rail column scales Y 1 -> 0 from the bottom origin, once on load; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; resting state leaves the rail visible.

motion.name: chip-color
motion.purpose: Terminus chip fill/ring changes when a target is chosen. Score figures never animate.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Page padding 16 -> 24px; header shows display name.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Student route becomes strip map left + 22rem sticky departure board right.

narrative.overview:
The term is a rail line the student rides. Every graded piece is a station, each unit is its own coloured line, the exams are interchanges, and the ride ends at the grade the student is aiming for. The site is a transit diagram printed on midnight enamel: porcelain ink for words and station rings, four line inks for the routes, and the stretch the student has already travelled lit a little brighter, with a soft neon bleed. It stands in for the usual summary cards, percentage rings and progress bars, which this system does not use.

Density is operational. Most students read it on a phone in the evening or between classes, and the teacher enters scores for a 30 to 35 student room at a desk. So the map is calm and the figures do the talking. Scores sit in a condensed transit face with tabular numerals, right-aligned, and they never move. The one piece of motion is the line drawing itself in once when the page loads.

Dark is the default and a light theme sits one toggle away in the header. Light is the same map printed on paper: navy ink replaces porcelain, the glow is switched off, and the line inks deepen to hold contrast on white. No glass, no blur, no gradients, in either theme.
keyCharacteristics: Midnight enamel ground (dark default), porcelain ink, and a light paper theme on the same tokens.
Four line inks (scarlet, cobalt, amber, green) given to units in order. Exams ride porcelain.
Filled disc = graded, hollow porcelain ring = not yet graded, and both always come with words.
Barlow Semi Condensed for signage and every figure (tabular, lining); Anuphan for all Thai and UI text.
Flat surfaces with 2px porcelain sign borders. The only light effect is a neon bleed on graded rails.
Numbers stay still. The rail draws in once on load.

rules.name: The Inherited Palette Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's slate, white, red, green, amber and blue-700 utilities are theme tokens. `globals.css` rebinds each of them (`--color-slate-800: var(--c-slate-800)` and so on) inside `@theme inline`, and defines the values twice: once on `:root` (dark) and once on `:root[data-theme="light"]`. In the dark theme slate is inverted, so slate-50 is the enamel ground, slate-800 is porcelain ink and `white` is raised enamel. Every existing page written with `bg-white`, `text-slate-800` or `border-slate-200` therefore changes theme without edits. Write new UI in those same utility names, or in `line-*` / `porcelain`, and never in raw colour values.

rules.name: The Line Ink Rule
rules.body: Line inks belong to units, cycling scarlet, cobalt, amber, green in unit order. Exams ride porcelain. A line ink can mark a rail, a line sign, a glyph or the active-tab underline. It never sets body text and never fills a large surface.

rules.name: The Amber Carries Dark Ink Rule
rules.body: Any text sitting on line-amber uses Sign Ink, in both themes.

rules.name: The Transit Figure Rule
rules.body: Every score, maximum, count and grade uses `font-sign` plus `.tnum` (tabular and lining numerals), so digits line up in columns. Thai words always stay in Anuphan, even when they sit inside a figure line (for example "ชิ้น").

rules.name: The Readable Score Rule
rules.body: A score is never smaller than 1.25rem and never below ink-primary on its own row. Missing scores show an en dash in ink-faint next to the maximum. They never show a zero.

rules.name: The Glow Belongs to the Route Rule
rules.body: Neon bleed marks where the student has been, and nowhere else. Cards, buttons, text and hover states do not glow. No glass, no blur, no gradients.

dos: Do write colour through the remapped Tailwind names (`bg-white`, `bg-slate-50`, `text-slate-800`, `border-slate-200`, `text-amber-700`) or the `line-*` / `porcelain` utilities, so a surface follows the theme toggle with no extra work.
Do add any new hue to both the `:root` and `:root[data-theme="light"]` blocks and bind it in `@theme inline`, in OKLCH.
Do set every number in `font-sign` with `.tnum`, right-aligned, with the maximum in ink-muted after a slash.
Do pair every station state with words. A hollow ring always comes with "ยังไม่มีคะแนน" (no score yet).
Do assign line inks by unit order (scarlet, cobalt, amber, green, then repeat) and put exams on porcelain.
Do keep the glow limited to graded rails and station discs, driven by `--glow-strength`.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. The rail reveal is the only load animation.
donts: Don't use glass, blur or gradients.
Don't animate, count up or re-flow score figures. Numbers never move.
Don't fall back on summary cards, percentage rings or progress bars for student progress. The line map replaces them.
Don't hard-code hex or oklch values, or Tailwind's stock palette, in components. They will not follow the theme.
Don't put light text on amber. Use Sign Ink.
Don't add steps, animation or layout weight to the teacher's score-entry flow. It must stay as fast as it is now.
Don't show a grade before every piece is scored. Until then, the terminus is the student's chosen target, labelled as one.
